title: Working from Home
description: Four recordings about working from home: a radio interview, a chat between colleagues, a podcast with tips and a message from a manager.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · A radio interview
parts.intro: You will hear a radio presenter, Carla, interviewing a designer called Mark.

script.speaker: Carla
script.text: Today we're talking about working from home. My guest is Mark, a graphic designer who has worked from his flat for six years. Mark, what's the best thing about it?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Definitely the freedom. I start when I want, and I don't spend two hours a day on a crowded train. I used to leave the house at seven and get back at seven. Now I use that time to go running.

script.speaker: Carla
script.text: Is there a downside?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Yes, loneliness. Some days I speak to nobody except the postman. At first, I found that really hard.

script.speaker: Carla
script.text: How did you deal with it?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: I joined a shared office two days a week. It's not expensive, about eighty pounds a month, and I meet other freelancers there. We have lunch together on Fridays.

script.speaker: Carla
script.text: And what about distractions at home? The washing, the television...

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Oh, I used to be terrible. I'd watch one programme just for a minute and lose a whole morning. Now I have a rule: the television doesn't go on before six.

script.speaker: Carla
script.text: Do you have a separate room for work?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Not really. I work at the kitchen table, and I tidy everything away at half past five. That helps my brain to switch off.

parts.title: Part 2 · Two colleagues
parts.intro: You will hear two colleagues, Tom and Mai, talking about Mai's new home office.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Hi, Mai. How's the new home office going? Your manager said you've been working from home since Monday.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: It's OK, but my back hurts already. I'm using a dining chair, and it's not comfortable.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: You should buy a proper office chair. The company pays up to one hundred pounds for equipment, you know.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Really? Nobody told me! Do I need to send a receipt?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Yes, send it to the finance team by email. But don't wait too long. You must do it within a month.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Thanks. The other problem is the noise. My neighbour is building a new kitchen, and the drill starts at eight every morning.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Ouch. Could you try headphones? I use the ones with noise cancelling, and they work well.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: I'll think about it. They look expensive. Maybe the company can pay for those too.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Perhaps not, but ask. By the way, are you coming to the office on Thursday for the team meeting?

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Yes, I wouldn't miss it. Honestly, I miss chatting with everybody at lunch.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: We miss you too. Right, I have to go. I have a video call in two minutes.

parts.title: Part 3 · A podcast
parts.intro: You will hear Priya, the host of a podcast about working from home.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Welcome to Work Smart, the podcast for people who work from home. I'm Priya, and in today's episode I'm sharing my five best tips for staying productive.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Tip one: have a morning routine. Get dressed, even if you're not leaving the house. I know it's tempting to work in your pyjamas, but research shows that wearing real clothes puts you in a working mood.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Tip two: plan your day the night before. Write down three important tasks, not ten. If you finish all three, anything else is a bonus.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Tip three: take regular breaks. I use a simple rule: work for fifty minutes, then rest for ten. Stand up, drink water, look out of the window. Don't check your phone, because that isn't really a rest.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Tip four is about your space. Even a small corner is fine, but make sure it has good light. Try to sit near a window if you can.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: And tip five: finish on time. Many people who work from home end up working longer, because the office is always there. Decide your finishing time, and then close your laptop.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Remember, working from home is a skill, and like any skill, it gets easier with practice.

parts.title: Part 4 · A message from the manager
parts.intro: You will hear a voicemail message from a manager, Greg, to his team.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: Hello, team, it's Greg. I'm leaving this message for everyone, because I'll be in meetings all day and can't answer the phone.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: First, thank you for the way you've adapted to our new working from home policy. The first month has gone better than I expected.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: From next week, we'll try a new system. Everyone will work from home on Mondays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays, and come to the office on Thursdays and Fridays. If you have a problem with those days, please speak to me by the end of this week.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: The big team meeting will stay on Thursday at ten, in the large meeting room on the third floor. We'll also have a short online meeting every Monday at half past nine. It's only fifteen minutes, so please be on time.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: Also, the technology team has sent a survey about your home internet. It takes five minutes to complete, and it's important, so please do it before Friday.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: Finally, a reminder that your computers must be locked when you're away from them, even at home. Security is everyone's job.

script.speaker: Greg
script.text: That's all. Speak soon, and have a good week.
